newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah soft on regional weakness.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah soft on regional weakness.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was soft against the dollar in slow late trading on Thursday.
Dealers said the rupiah was driven lower on regional weakness, breaking the support level of 2,600 after offshore players sold rupiah for dollars ahead of the weekend.
"There was not much activity in the afternoon. It's still the regional factor which determines the market," one European bank dealer said, adding dollar liquidity seemed to improve.
Overnight dollars fell to seven percent from 10.0 percent in the morning. Spot rupiah was at 2,600/05 at 0930 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,575/85.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,602.6/07.6 and 2,597/2,600, respectively.
However, the fall of the rupiah did not make the market nervous because it was still within the range the central bank has said it is comfortable with in an environment of regional uncertainty.
The bank said after reaching a low of 2,663 rupiah against the dollar on July 21, the currency had in recent days reached a normal level of between 2,555 and 2,610 rupiah.
It said the range was normal under current conditions.
But the European bank dealer said it was not clear whether the bank would intervene if rates fall out of the range.
"It's regional rather than rupiah trading. You have to look to other currencies in the region before you can have a view on the local market," one local bank dealer said earlier.

One currency strategist said he expected the instability in Thailand to continue because the implementation of an IMF programme would bring short-term pain. Thailand was seeking IMF assistance to turn around its ailing economy.
"You are not going to see a miraculous recovery tomorrow. Nobody is expecting that. It's going to be some months down the road before you see things stabilising," he said.
"The concern would dissipate once the pressure point in the region, which is Thailand, shows sign of stability. But that stability may not come about for six to eight months," he said.
The central bank continued its tight grip on the money market by keeping short-term rates expensive to contain speculative dollar buying.
However, a well prepared market facing the month-end pushed overnight rates down to the central bank limit of 14.0 percent from 19.0 percent in the early morning.
The high short-term rates and cheap swap rates enabled banks with sufficient net open positions to proceed with their profitable arbitrage deals.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at 0.2/0.3.

The central bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Bank Indonesia remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market. Dealers said swaps were off an early high but were more expensive than Wednesday.
One-month swap was at 15.0/16.5, two at 33.0/35.0, three at 50.0/54.0 and six at 106.0/110.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but raised the conversion band to 2,575/2,623 on Thursday from 2,559/2,607 on Wednesday.
